key_insight: DICE ensembles frozen pathology foundation models and uses their disagreement, refined by deep mutual learning, to estimate uncertainty while also improving patch-level abnormality localization.
clinical_relevance: It may help pathologists and decision-support systems identify when a whole-slide image prediction is unreliable, especially under out-of-distribution cases.
method: Ensembles K frozen pathology foundation models in a plug-and-play setup.
Uses model disagreement as a proxy for uncertainty.
Applies deep mutual learning to align ensemble members and tighten uncertainty estimates.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports evaluation on three whole-slide image benchmarks, with reliable uncertainty estimates and performance that matches or outperforms strong baselines for classification, calibration, and localization.
watch_item: The approach depends on multiple pretrained foundation models and careful ensemble calibration, so added compute and deployment complexity may limit practical adoption.
paper_title: Uncertainty Estimation in Pathology Foundation Models via Deep Mutual Learning
